column3: The Hebrew repeats the death statement after describing the sons’ approach; BSB states their death once.
The Hebrew says not to enter “at every time” and calls the inner area “the holy place”; BSB says not to enter “freely” and specifies “the Most Holy Place.”
The Hebrew calls the bull “a son of the herd”; BSB says “a young bull.”
The Hebrew explicitly puts the linen undergarments “on his flesh” and later says to wash “his flesh”; BSB omits the first location phrase and uses “bathe himself” for the washing.

The Hebrew explicitly names Aaron and says the lot “came up upon” the goat; BSB uses “he” and “chosen by lot.”
The Hebrew says to make atonement “over it,” followed by the purpose of sending it away; BSB expresses atonement “by sending it.”

The Hebrew has an unnamed subject and repeats “the mercy seat” twice; BSB names Aaron and replaces the second occurrence with “it.”

The Hebrew says “the holy place” and describes the tent as dwelling with them “in the midst of their impurities”; BSB specifies “the Most Holy Place” and turns the final location phrase into “because it is surrounded by their impurities.”
The Hebrew uses an unnamed “he” and says “the holy place”; BSB supplies Aaron’s name and specifies “the Most Holy Place.”

The Hebrew changes from singular active “he shall take out” to plural active “they shall burn with fire”; BSB uses passive verbs for both actions and specifies “the Most Holy Place” for “the holy place.”

The Hebrew says to afflict “your souls”; BSB says to “humble yourselves.”
The Hebrew has active “he shall make atonement”; BSB uses passive “atonement will be made.”
